question.problem:
Lucy wants to make a cake and is going to buy some fruit to decorate. How much would it cost her to buy $\frac{1}{8}$ of a pound of strawberries?

| Item | Price |
| --- | --- |
| Peach | $$1.75/\text{lb}$ |
| Strawberries | $$2.00/\text{lb}$ |

current_example.problem:
Micah is going to the store to buy some sunflower seeds. How much would it cost to buy $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of a pound of sunflower seeds?

| Item | Price |
| --- | --- |
| Pumpkin Seeds | $\[math] 8 / \text{lb}$ |
| Sunflower Seeds | $\[/math] 5 / \text{lb}$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
The price of sunflower seeds is $\[math] 5 / \text{lb}.$ To find the cost of  $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of a pound of sunflower seeds, we multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\times \frac{1}{4} & =\frac{5}{1}\times \frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{5\times 1}{1\times 4} \\  & =\frac{5}{4} \\  & =5÷4 \\  & =1.25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it would cost $\[/math] 1.25$ to buy $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of a pound of sunflower seeds.
